title: Pimientos de Padrón: Blistered Peppers with Sea Salt
summary: Small green Padrón peppers blistered in a smoking-hot pan until charred and just tender, then finished with olive oil and flaky sea salt.

ingredients.item: Padrón peppers, rinsed and dried thoroughly

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Pat the peppers completely dry with a clean towel. Any water left on them makes the hot oil spit and steams the skins instead of blistering them.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the neutral oil in a large cast-iron pan over high heat until it just begins to smoke. A very hot pan chars the skins before the flesh turns soft.

steps.title: Blister
steps.text: Add the peppers in a single layer, in two batches if needed, and leave them alone for 30 seconds, until blackened in spots underneath. Then toss and turn them for 1-2 minutes more, until blistered all over and just softened but still bright green.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Tip the peppers onto a plate, drizzle with the olive oil and scatter with the flaky salt. Eat at once, holding them by the stem.

tips: Crowding the pan is the usual mistake: the peppers steam and go limp. Cook in batches.
Use flaky salt; its crunch is part of the dish.
Open a window or turn on the extractor, since the smoking oil can set off alarms.
Shishito peppers work the same way.
storage: Best eaten straight from the pan. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days and are good chopped into eggs or salads. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
